items.title: South Korea to recall Ukraine envoy in diplomatic row over POWs
items.description: South Korea recalls envoy from Kyiv amid diplomatic tensions over alleged transfer of North Korean soldiers to Seoul.

items.title: Strike on Ukrainian public bus leaves 30 dead as blackouts worsen in Kyiv
items.description: Russian strikes in eastern Ukraine have killed 30 people and injured at least 18, according to authorities. The attacks included a strike on a public bus and have worsened power outages in Kyiv.

items.title: Dozens Killed In Russian Strike On Passenger Buses In Kramatorsk
items.description: Dozens of people were killed in a Russian strike on the Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk on October 8, according to local authorities, a day after another deadly barrage killed at least 25 people across Ukraine.

items.title: Eritrean troops reportedly enter Ethiopia’s Tigray region
items.description: Eritrean troops have deployed in Ethiopia's northern Tigray region, multiple sources said Wednesday, threatening to turn an internal conflict into a wider regional war. items.title: EU Lifts Belarus-Related Sanctions on Russian Billionaire Gutseriev – RFE/RL
items.description: The billionaire remains subject to separate EU sanctions linked to Russia’s war in Ukraine.

items.title: 'Every day there is killing': Palestinians in Gaza face Israeli strikes despite ceasefire as peace deal stalls
items.description: Many Palestinians are still living in cramped tent cities, with the US plan to end the war largely stalled.

items.title: In Somalia, war cuts off aid for entire populations threatened by famine
items.description: Violent clashes between rival government factions have further worsened the food crisis affecting nearly seven million Somalis. Fleeing drought and hunger, refugees continue to pour into camps where humanitarian organizations have a presence, as the Islamist group Al-Shabab has banned them from certain areas.

items.title: In Ukraine, holding on to childhood in a time of war
items.description: As war in Ukraine continues into its fifth year, some children have only known war. The Monitor revisits three young families striving to live full lives amid Russia’s military invasion.

items.title: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Turkey: Could the Mecca defense pact become a game changer in the war against the Houthis in Yemen?
items.description: Pakistan and Turkey have agreed to provide "practical measures" to defend Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks. Could a new alliance reshape the war against the Houthis in Yemen?

items.title: 5 Children, Including Three 1-Year-Old Boys, Among 19 Killed in Russian Strike on Pryluky
items.description: Five children, including three 1-year-old boys, are among 19 people killed in a Russian missile strike on a residential building in Pryluky, northern Ukraine. The attack was part of a massive overnight barrage that killed at least 25 people nationwide and injured dozens more.

items.title: Djibouti faces ‘overlapping emergencies’ as Yemen’s refugee exodus continues
items.description: Djibouti is facing “overlapping emergencies” as refugees fleeing the conflict in Yemen arrive on its shores while migrants continue to travel in the opposite direction, the UN migration agency (IOM) warned on Tuesday.
